newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends up sharply on funds, options expry.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends up sharply on funds, options expry.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures surged in late dealings and ended sharply higher on fund buying tied to options-related arbitrage trading, traders said.
"This is not fundamental," said Skip Searcy of FIMAT Futures. "There was a lot of buying against expiring options."
The CBOT March options expired at 1201 CST leaving open the potential for a late race to the $3.70 strike price in the nearby March futures contract.
"Stops were hit above $3.70 the March," a trader said.
Traders said funds bought roughly 10 million bushels.
Volatile moves in corn and soybean futures led to a mixed picture for CBOT wheat futures through much of the session with commercials and speculators on each side of the market and for small amounts.

But the volume mounted as did the bullish momentum into the close with Griffin Trading and Rosenthal Collins each said purchasing roughly two million bushels of March during the waning 30 minutes of action.
Wheat closed nine to 10-1/2 cents higher, with March up 9-1/4 at $3.73 per bushel and new-crop July 9-3/4 cents higher at $3.63.
Wheat export news was about as expected and new crop July, especially in the Kansas City hard red winter market, was pressured by moisture being received in the U.S. winter wheat growing region.
USDA early Friday said U.S. net export sales of wheat during the week ended Feb 13 totaled 287,200 tonnes, near the high end of expectations for 250,000 to 300,000 tonnes.
But other export news was sparse with Taiwan setting a tender for 69,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat Thursday and the Philippines overnight bought 35,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat.

Sources in Sydney overnight also reported greater volume in the Australian wheat futures market but there was no fresh fundamental input. The stronger Australian market followed the rise in CBOT late Thursday, led by the surge in soybeans and rally in corn, they said.
Technicians early Friday cited the longer term four and 20-day moving averages for wheat as bearish for the March but bullish for May and July.

The short term nine day relative strength index for the March closed at 61.8 percent after hovering in neutral territory of about 50 percent or so through midsession. The market views an RSI of 70 or more as overbought and 30 or less as oversold.
First support for the March was $3.60-1/2 and second support was $3.55. The session low for March was $3.61.
First resistance was $3.66 and second resistance was $3.71-1/2. The session high for March was $3.75-1/2.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 20,000 contracts, above the 16,958 traded Thursday.

In wheat options, Tenco Inc sold 250 July $3.50 puts at 16-1/4 to 16-1/2 cents, bought 250 July $4.00 calls at 6-1/4 to 6-1/2 cents, bought 150 July $3.80 calls at nine to 9-1/2 cents, bought 100 July $3.70 calls at 11-1/2 to 12 cents and bought 100 July $3.60 calls at 14-1/2 to 15 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 4,500 contracts, about the same as the 4,512 traded Thursday.
